target_customer: Non-US and US online founders, creators and ecommerce sellers who need a US LLC or C-Corp, EIN, registered agent, bookkeeping and tax filings
problem: Forming a US company, opening a bank account and keeping up with compliance and taxes is slow and confusing, especially for founders without a US Social Security number.
business_model: Subscription bundle (plans from $297 per year plus state fees) with formation, compliance, bookkeeping and tax services, plus a formation API for businesses
product_category: Business formation and back-office compliance platform

founders.name: Arjun Mahadevan
founders.background_notes: Prior employer from the TechCrunch seed article of 2021-11-15. Education not found in any opened source. The YC page lists him as the only founder.

founders.name: JP Pincheira
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CTO in the TechCrunch seed article of 2021-11-15; the article gives no background. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Stripe Atlas
competitors.what: Online incorporation kit for Delaware companies aimed at founders worldwide, which added LLC formation in April 2018
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the cited article
competitors.funding_then: Product of Stripe, a well funded payments company

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software on top of state filings and partners such as banks and tax preparers. The TechCrunch article says it relied on partners for services it could not provide in house, and it launched an MVP quickly.

defensibility.rationale: Formation itself is a commodity offered by Stripe Atlas and others. Recurring compliance and tax work creates some switching costs once a company is on the platform.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe Atlas already served international founders in 2020 and kept operating. No source shows an incumbent absorbing the wedge, and doola kept raising through 2024.

market_need_then: The TechCrunch article describes demand from founders without a US Social Security number, and says hundreds of companies had formed LLCs with doola by November 2021.

identity.logo: Wordmark; the site page does not describe the design
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, reassuring and plain spoken; the page title plays on the spelling Do'ers

rebrands.why: Not stated; TechCrunch says the company started as StartPack and later rebranded

brand_strength.rationale: A short distinctive name and a clear voice, but searches found no press about the brand, mascot, merch or community.

pivots.to: StartPack, later renamed doola (company formation and back office)

outcome_analysis: doola pivoted from an earlier idea into LLC formation for global founders, raised a $3M seed in 2021, an $8M Series A and a strategic HubSpot Ventures round in January 2024, and states $13M raised in total. The CEO told TechCrunch the business was growing profitably on unit economics, and the company reports founders in 175 plus countries. Formation is easy to copy, so the later push into banking, bookkeeping and tax APIs is the path to a durable position. No shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Series A date conflict: an aggregator (startupintros) dates it 2022-11 while the January 2024 company release says the HubSpot round came less than one year after the $8M Series A, so the date is left null. TechCrunch gives $3.6M total raised in 2021, so about $0.6M before the seed is unaccounted. The company states $13M total in January 2024. Aggregator figures such as $1M for the HubSpot round are unverified. Outcome search found no acquisition, layoffs or shutdown. Competitor search found only Stripe Atlas with a dated source; Firstbase results were about a different remote work company. Founder education not found. The YC launch posts listed on the YC page are for later products and were not opened.
